title: How Acne Works
summary: Josh and Chuck explain how acne forms, starting with the layers of skin and the constant turnover of skin cells, then the role of sebum, sebaceous glands and hair follicles. They cover the sequence from clogged pores to whiteheads, blackheads, pustules, papules and nodules, plus comedones. They discuss milia in babies, pre-pubertal acne, rosacea, and myths about diet, genetics, dirt and makeup. Treatments covered include benzoyl peroxide, salicylic acid, moisturizing, gentle washing, birth control pills, antibiotics, chemical peels, lasers and professional extraction. The episode closes with a super Stuff audiobook plug, listener mail from author Tyler Davis, and corrections about failsafe and the buttered bread myth.

segments.title: Opening banter and skin care interest
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck banter about skin care articles they wrote, facts about lip skin thickness, licking lips, and Chuck's nose pimple.

segments.title: Skin layers and skin cell turnover
segments.summary: The hosts describe the skin as the largest organ, its three layers (epidermis, dermis, subcutaneous layer), and how skin cells are born in lower layers, move outward, die, and are shed at a rate of tens of millions per day. Dead cells mix with sebum and lipids to form a waterproof, bacteria-resistant barrier.

segments.title: Hair follicles, sebaceous glands and clogging
segments.summary: Hair follicles connect to sebaceous glands that release sebum, which is why adolescents and men tend to have more oil. When too many dead cells or too much sebum block the pore, bacteria such as P. acnes feed on the sebum and cause inflammation.

segments.title: Whiteheads, blackheads, pustules, papules and nodules
segments.summary: Comedones are explained: whiteheads are closed and blackheads are open, with the black being oxidized pigment rather than dirt. The hosts discuss pustules (zits), papules, nodules, and distinguish cysts. They note the terminology confusion from the American Academy of Dermatology.

segments.title: Milia, pre-pubertal acne and rosacea
segments.summary: Milia are small white bumps common in newborns that usually clear on their own. Pre-pubertal acne appears in young children from early androgen production and warrants a doctor visit. Rosacea affects the nose and face with flushing and bouts, and is often mistaken for signs of heavy drinking.

segments.title: Myths: diet, genetics, dirt and makeup
segments.summary: Diet is said by most doctors to be largely a myth, though insulin effects and omega-3 foods are discussed as possible influences. Genetics matters but less than expected. Dirt does not cause acne. Makeup, especially non-comedogenic issues and leaving makeup on overnight, can cause breakouts.

segments.title: Acne treatments
segments.summary: Over-the-counter treatments for regular acne vulgaris are mainly benzoyl peroxide and salicylic acid. Dry skin can worsen breakouts, so moisturizing helps. Gentle washing, showering after exercise, antibiotics, birth control pills, chemical peels, and laser treatment are discussed, along with the warning against squeezing and professional extraction by estheticians.

segments.title: Stress, personality and body acne
segments.summary: Loose clothing and stress reduction are recommended. The hosts joke about a serotonin transporter gene study framed as type L and type S personalities. Back, chest, and buttock bumps are briefly mentioned.

segments.title: Super Stuff audiobook plug
segments.summary: The hosts promote The Super Stuff Guide to Happiness audiobook on iTunes.

segments.title: Listener mail from Tyler Davis and corrections
segments.summary: Author Tyler Davis writes from abroad about hearing the show on a flight and thanks the hosts for mentioning his book. The hosts define hinky and issue corrections on failsafe design and the buttered bread myth, with Chuck disagreeing that bread always lands butter-side down.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts invite corrections and contact through Twitter, Facebook and email, and promote the Stuff from the Future video podcast.
